account:
Today I have kept my scheduled rounds: morning office business, the ten o'clock mill inspection, lunch at home, council letters, tea with my neighbour, and now the late-afternoon office appointment. At the mill I counted eighty-two hay bales in the sales chest, but no responsible worker gave me a condition report. The secretary says no new correspondence or requests have reached her; her enquiries have also failed to identify where the accounts ledger or incoming council letters are normally kept. That gap remains unresolved.

The unusual town conversation concerns a possible bridge or port change associated with the bakery. Several townsfolk repeated it, mentioning the baker and freight, but I have neither seen a proposal nor received firsthand confirmation of an actual change. My neighbour likewise heard only vague remarks. I cannot tell whether this is a real plan or circulating speculation, much less what its purpose would be.

An eighteen o'clock community gathering in the great hall is confirmed with the innkeeper. Freight is here at the office, and the secretary says he will escort me at seventeen forty-five. I know of no confirmed connection between that gathering and the rumours. The builder and innkeeper heard my recent office greeting, though I could not see them from where I stood. For now I am waiting for the escort and keeping the gathering appointment, without treating the bakery rumours as established business.
